# Household

> Household runs terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex) as personal assistants you talk to in Telegram. Each agent
> ("pet") lives in its own microVM; a daemon on the user's Mac or Linux machine proxies all its traffic through an
> allowlist and puts API keys into requests on the way out, so agents only ever see placeholders.

To set up or manage Household for a user, install the `household` agent skill and follow it:

- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add underwear/household && claude plugin install household@household`
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add underwear/household && codex plugin add household@household`

Secrets (agent keys, bot tokens) go from the user straight to the `house` CLI through stdin, never through the agent.

## Docs

- [Setup](https://github.com/underwear/household/blob/main/plugins/household/skills/household/install.md): requirements, installing, agent keys (Claude subscription or API key, ChatGPT subscription or OpenAI API key), the Telegram bot, running as a service
- [Operating](https://github.com/underwear/household/blob/main/plugins/household/skills/household/operate.md): pets, network and secrets, scouts and capabilities, updates and migrations, backups
- [Debugging](https://github.com/underwear/household/blob/main/plugins/household/skills/household/debug.md): where to look when a pet, scout or channel does not work
- [Skill overview](https://github.com/underwear/household/blob/main/plugins/household/skills/household/SKILL.md): concepts and the rules an agent follows

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/underwear/household): TypeScript on Bun; `house --help` lists every command
